key: But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD.
s: Told by Doeg of the help given at Nob, Saul orders his guard to kill the priests; Rashi, on 22:17, reads the refusal as the guards expounding Scripture to hold that a command to sin need not be obeyed, even a king’s.

evidence.gloss: Would not: they expounded the limiting words of Scripture (Joshua 1:18): ‘Whosoever he be that shall rebel against thy commandment [shall be put to death]’; one might think this holds even for a command to transgress, so Scripture says ‘only’.

reason: Key verse verbatim, the second sentence of 22:17 (verse.js ok, ref 1 Samuel 22:17 and at [253,17] match). Packet read on 22:17 and around it (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David). Rashi on ‘would not’ says they expounded the limiting words of Joshua 1:18: the death penalty for rebelling against the ruler’s command might seem to hold even for a command to transgress, so Scripture says ‘only’ to exclude it; Radak repeats the same derash. The reading ‘a command to sin need not be obeyed, even a king’s’ stays within that. Plain sense states Doeg’s report and Saul’s order to kill the priests in one plain clause. entry-check ok.
